newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares end lower as market seeks balance.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares end lower as market seeks balance.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped a fraction on Wednesday as the market continued to find its balance after dizzying record highs in late February were corrected this week.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index slid 0.28 points to close at 400.26, from its rise to 400.54 points on Tuesday. Turnover was 114.2 million pounds ($33.6 million).

"There are no fundamentals behind the movement. Most of the investors in the market are small time buyers and they are leading the market now. They are scooping up small bundles of shares," said Youssef Khalil, broker at EFG/Hermes.

Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries stocks saw most of the action, with 11 million pounds of turnover. Its shares rose 5.3 pounds to close at 111.3, on rumours that the firm would soon be the target of a global depositary receipt offering (GDR).
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the next most active share with 9.1 million pounds in trade. Shares inched up 0.6 pounds to close at 489 pounds.
The cement sector was also active, brokers said. "A lot of demand was on the cement sector, which is a liquid stock so it's not surprising," said Fabienne Gimenez of brokers EFG-Hermes.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was a hard-hitting share in 7.9 million turnover, but its share edged down 2.4 to 90. Amriya Cement was also busy and ended lower 3.15 pounds at 84.85 pounds.

Banks, which helped fuel the bourse's recent rises, slowed down and ended mostly lower. Misr International Bank/MIBANK, which will offer GDRs soon, ended 2.89 pounds down at 765 in heavy trade and Commercial International Bank, which issued the country's first GDR, fell 24.1 to 875.9 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 655.15 from 652.15 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms was also up, at 267.14 from 268.25.
Out of the 88 shares traded, 40 gained, 34 lost and 14 ended the day unchanged.
